newsitem.title: UK: Euro fuel markets end day trading unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Euro fuel markets end day trading unchanged.

text.p: European barge markets lost their early strength to trade unchanged on Thursday as bunker demand faded away, while low sulphur fuel buyers continued hesitant, traders said.
After a deal at $81 fob a tonne for high sulphur in Rotterdam, barge offers rose to $83 a tonne. One deal was heard at $82 as offer levels slid lower and business died away.
Bunker demand was reported healthy in the morning. Low sulphur barges were as usual thinly discussed but prices were agreed to be standing nominally around $97 a tonne.
Russian material was beginning to weigh on the ARA market, traders said, though buyers were still cautious over quality and the effect on prices has not yet been catastrophic.
Low sulphur swaps were fractionally weaker, reflecting the market's rather stilted character, traders said.

A German trader was heard to have bought the British barrels sold to a U.S. refiner by a dealer last Friday. Las week's deal at $95 a tonne fob surprised the market so much no other material has been traded since.
The German trader was heard to have paid the average of June quotes plus a small premium and was believed to be taking the material to Puerto Rico.
"This material is just getting passed around and nothing else is happening," said one dealer.
Small parcels of one percent were being offered into Italy but the supply was generally considered thin.
